cards.label: C001
cards.hyp: Is the thruster a generic Chinese part, and are its listed dimensions real?
cards.note: → CAD v2.0: kick-up mount on the transom (decision 0004); coupon → C005
cards.notes: FAILS_AND_FIXES draft: 143. The thruster is taller than the draft (C001, 08.10) → duct OD 72.27 mm (box drawing says 77 mm, 112 mm long), frame face → prop axis 47.10 mm, frame 9.68 mm thick, 4 brass inserts, screws M4 (thread 3.93 mm) × 28.4 mm from outside, cable Ø5.62 mm with 4 wires (black + red thick, white + yellow thin), mass 201 / 206 g. CAD v1.9 stern pad was a guess (44 × 44, tp_z 25, tp_pitch 20, M3): wrong screw size, wrong pattern, and a 72 mm duct cannot be fully under water at a 42 mm draft. Hole pitch c-c 34.8–35.3 × 15.2–16.0 from four readings. Decision (Teddy): kick-up mount on the transom, hinge above the waterline. Next: test coupon 50 × 30 × 5 PETG, 4 × Ø4.5 at 35.0 × 15.6. Lesson: measure the bought part before drawing its mount.
cards.result: duct Ø72.27 × 112 (box says 77), mounting face 47.10 above the axis, frame 9.68, M4 (3.93) at 34.8–35.3 × 15.2–16.0, 201/206 g, cable Ø5.62 with 4 wires. Listing dimensions are not real; a 72 mm duct does not fit under a 42 mm waterline on a flat pad
cards.title: Cuifati thruster: dimensions, bolt pattern, mass

cards.label: C002
cards.hyp: 3 equal pairs under 1 Ω = motor phases (external ESC needed)
cards.note: → C006: 9 V with 0.10 A limit in a bucket
cards.notes: From the listing (same text under other brands, not confirmed for this unit): PWM 50 Hz, 1500 µs = stop, 1500→2000 forward, 1500→1000 reverse; 12–14.8 V, up to 13 A, under 8 A average at 12 V; no BEC; do not run dry > 10 s. Logic level and arming not documented. Meter: EMOS MD-220.
cards.result: 4 wires, not 3. No shorts. red↔black ~1.0 kΩ; yellow↔black 316 Ω / 8.86 kΩ reversed; white↔black 911 Ω / ~50 Ω reversed. Asymmetric = electronics inside (ESC). Red +, black −; yellow probably signal, white probably signal ground
cards.title: Thruster: the 4 wires, ESC or phases (no 12 V)

cards.label: C007
cards.hyp: 0 drops inside after 20 min (dry paper); floats upright, heel < 5°; draft at own mass and with +1 kg recorded (calibrates 8.9 mm/kg)
cards.note: Weigh the section first (kitchen scale, brim peeled off). Paper on the floor inside. 20 min in the tub, then with a 1 kg weight in the middle. Mark the waterline, caliper afterwards. 4K video from the side, 5 s before/after. Target: R1a. PREDICTION (CAD, one hull_fore section): waterplane 255 cm² (bow 150 × 100 parabolic + 155 × 100 straight) → 39.2 mm/kg. Own mass 345 g → draft ~13.5 mm; +1 kg → ~53 mm. The 4 joint holes in the aft bulkhead sit at z 75 / 105 (Ø3.4, lowest edge 73.3) → 20 mm above the +1 kg waterline. Do NOT add more than 1.5 kg extra or they go under. Put the weight in the middle (heel). Check: two full hulls (2 × 610) = 1120 cm² → 8.9 mm/kg, so the measured mm/kg here × 255/1120 should come back to ~8.9.
cards.result: PASS 11.10 15:35. Floats upright with no visible heel. DRY inside after ~15 min in the water, most of it loaded to ~64 mm mid-hull, which is deeper and stricter on the walls than empty. This was not a separate 20 min empty soak. PRE-TEST 15:12: mass 323 g with brim and supports off (the screen's 345.0 g includes brim, supports and purge). Length ≈ 30.5 cm (CAD 305). Bottom → lower edge of the lowest joint hole 73.26 (CAD 73.3). EMPTY: draft 12.99 mm (caliper depth rod, mid-hull) vs 12.7 predicted → waterplane 249 cm² vs CAD 255 (−2.5 %) → two full hulls ≈ 9.1 mm/kg instead of 8.9 (the 42 mm robot waterline holds within ~1 mm). LOADED: 2 bottles standing, 1374 g weighed (1000 ml aft compartment + 300 ml bow): draft 63.57 mid-hull → Δ 50.58 → 36.8 mm/kg vs 39.2 (−6 %). Most likely cause: trim. The 1 kg bottle sat ~78 mm aft of the waterplane centre (x ≈ 174 from the bow tip), so the stern went deeper and the mid-hull reading was a little forward of the centre. For a clean loaded point next time, read at the square aft end and 43 mm from the bow tip, then average. Margin loaded: ~10 mm to the joint holes mid-hull, less at the stern. Video IMG_1517: the tall bottle tipped over at ~10 s (high CG); the hull stayed afloat. Lessons: a low, centred weight (1 kg rice or sugar); weigh the load before it goes in. Media: C007_01–11 + captions.md in iCloud 01_Loops/C007_2026-10-11_bathtub (★ 01 empty afloat, 04 caliper 12.99, 05 loaded 63.57, 07 aft end, 10 loaded side view). C007_07 shows the stern waterline at ~70 mm, ~3–5 mm under the lowest joint-hole edge (estimated from the photo), so the stern sat ~6 mm deeper than mid-hull. That trim explains part of the 36.8 vs 39.2 mm/kg gap; the rest is caliper reading error on a floating hull. Pre-test photos added as C007_12–15 (15:07–15:10): 323 g; aft end (out of focus); hull height 119.70 (CAD 120); bottom → lowest joint-hole edge 73.26. The ruler photo (≈30.5 cm) is only in the chat.
cards.title: hull_fore in the bathtub: floats, leaks, draft

cards.label: C015
cards.hyp: Meter on GPIO39 (L RPWM) with RST held reads ≈ 3.3 V (ESP32-S3 boot pull-up); with 10 kΩ from GPIO39 to GND it reads < 0.8 V. GPIO40–42 read < 0.8 V in normal boot.
cards.note: Found in the T3 review. Do it BEFORE the first bts7960 bench run. DevKit on USB only, BTS7960 not connected. Meter DC V, GPIO39 → GND: (1) sketch running, (2) RST held, (3) BUT1 + RST held (download mode). Repeat for GPIO40, 41, 42. Then 10 kΩ GPIO39 → GND and repeat (2). Until this is closed: rocker in KILL whenever you flash or press reset, RUN only after the banner. The result decides 10 kΩ pull-downs on GPIO39–42 in pcb/carrier-revA/SPEC.md and on breadboards 1/2b (firmware/armini uses the same pins). Source: github.com/mcuw/esp32-s3-pinouts. Photo: meter display at each step, C015_NN.
cards.title: GPIO39 at reset: is the left BTS7960 RPWM pulled high during boot?

cards.label: C017
cards.hyp: Disc horn bolt circle 16.0 mm (holes opposite, centre to centre), holes take M2 through d2.4; the horn hub passes the d6.5 centre hole; the arm sits flat on the disc with all 4 screws in by hand.
cards.note: PRINTED 10.10 ~18:40: 20 min, 13.0 g (printer screen), orange PLA, external spool; clean first layer (video IMG_1412). First good print after the heat-break jam and the 140 °C nozzle issue. Next: step 3 (fit). TD-8120MG BODY re-measured 10.10 ~19:00 (8 photos, servo in the vise): length 40.40 (CAD pocket 40.5 → too tight), width 20.17 (pocket 20.4 ok), height 40.85 (CAD 40.7), bottom → ear plane 28.51 (CAD depth 28.0 → servo would bottom out before the ears seat), ear hole d4.05 (old note 4.34), 2 holes on one ear 9.65 apart (CAD 10), hole to hole across the top 48.14 (method unclear; CAD span 50.2 → re-measure: A = outside jaws closed on the inner edges, B = inside jaws opened on the outer edges, c-c = (A+B)/2). CAD update waits for that number. Disc horn not measured yet (not on the servo in the photos). 1) Before printing (30 s): caliper on the TD-8120MG metal disc horn — centre-to-centre of two OPPOSITE holes (CAD: 16.0 = 2 x disc_r 8, MEASURE) and the hole / screw size (CAD d2.4). Different → tell Claude, change disc_r / disc_d, export again. 2) Print build/arm_drive.stl (130 x 28 x 6 mm, ~19 g, ~30 min): PLA orange from the external spool, CFS off, 0.2 mm, 4 walls, 5 top/bottom, 40 % infill, flat, no supports, no brim. One piece first; the second only after the first fits. 3) Fit: 4 screws by hand, hub through the centre, arm flat, no rocking. Photo: caliper on the disc, the arm on the horn from above and from the side. CAD preset is servo_sel = TD8120 (bathtub test); ST3215 later. Do not commit the part = "arm_drive" line OpenSCAD wrote into AR-Mini_v1.scad (git checkout -- cad/openscad/AR-Mini_v1.scad).
cards.result: PASS 10.10 19:30 (7 photos). No metal disc in the TD-8120MG bag: the round BLACK PLASTIC disc horn (25T) was used. All 4 arm holes line up with a hole ring on the disc; the 4 bag screws go through the arm and bite into the disc; arm lies flat on the disc, level in the side photos. Disc ring: 13.75 mm across two opposite holes (inner edges) + hole d ~2.2 → c-c ~16, CAD disc_r 8 confirmed. Follow-ups, all closed 10.10: (1) disc pushed fully onto the spline + centre screw fitted (20:15); (2) case top → disc top 8.84 when seated (14.84 to the arm top) → CAD; (3) ear holes A 44.35 / B 52.16 → c-c 48.26 → CAD. Commits 6a5e449, 679779f, feb6f23. Photos C017_01–26 in iCloud.
cards.title: arm_drive (orange PLA) on the TD-8120MG disc horn: does it fit?

cards.label: C019
cards.hyp: The TD-8120MG drops into the 40.7 × 20.4 pocket by hand and its ears sit flat on the block face; all 4 M3 ear screws reach their inserts (48.26 × 9.65); arm_drive (on the disc) and arm_idler (on the 20.5 mm idler boss) lie in one plane ±0.5 mm; the coupler joins both arm ends without forcing; the linkage swings 45° → 215° by hand without touching the bracket or the hull.

Photos per side: bracket from above, servo in, linkage at 45° and at 215°, side view showing both arms in one plane.

cards.label: C025
cards.hyp: After `arm` the ESC accepts 1500 µs within 3 s (beeps); 1550 µs spins forward, 1450 µs reverse; at 1650 µs the current from 12.0 V stays under 3 A; full forward (2000 µs, on the LiPo) draws ≤ 8 A (listing); KILL or the dead-man stops the prop in < 0.5 s.
cards.note: Only after C006 and the `esc` env (C024). C006 tells whether the yellow wire idles above 3.6 V — if it does, do NOT connect it straight to GPIO1 (the ESP32-S3 is 3.3 V only): stop and ask Claude (level shifter). 1) Thruster in a bucket, duct fully under water, held down. 2) Jesverty 12.0 V, CC 3 A; meter in series (10 A jack). 3) `arm`, then 1550 / 1450 / 1600 / 1650 µs, 10 s each; write the current and the direction. 4) KILL rocker while spinning, time it on video. 5) Full power only on the LiPo through the inline fuse + 20 A slot, ≤ 5 s. Log with bench_log.py --card C025. Video from the side, 4K, prop visible.
cards.title: Thruster spins in a bucket: DevKit → ESC, forward and reverse

cards.label: C026
cards.hyp: Main switch OFF: 0 V on every fuse slot. Main switch ON from the Jesverty (12.0 V, CC 0.5 A): every slot reads 12.0 ±0.1 V, the fuse-block LEDs stay dark (no blown fuse), the MZHOU buck gives 5.00–5.25 V, idle current < 50 mA. Same on the LiPo: slots = pack voltage ±0.1 V.
cards.note: Wiring as in the hardware circuit diagram: XT60 → 30 A inline fuse → 50 A switch → fuse block (20 A ESCs, 15 A servo bus, 10 A BTS7960, 5 A logic/buck, 5 A spare), 14 AWG for everything above 10 A. Before any power: continuity meter — + to − must NOT beep anywhere; polarity marked on every lead. First power only from the Jesverty with CC 0.5 A (a short just limits, nothing burns). Then the LiPo. Nothing connected after the fuses yet. Photo of the wiring from above + the meter on each slot. Decides what goes into the power box later.
cards.title: Power chain on the bench, no loads: fuse → 50 A switch → fuse block → 5 V buck

cards.label: C027
cards.hyp: The `ladder` env reads v_bat within ±2 % of the multimeter at 10.0, 11.1 and 12.6 V (Jesverty into the 100k/33k divider); the leak probe in a glass of tap water sets leak=1 within 100 ms; the rocker in KILL sets kill=1 and in RUN kill=0.
cards.note: Sketch exists (T3, env `ladder`, PROTOCOL.md). Needs the 100k/33k 1 % resistors (BOM row 56, ordered). DevKit on USB, rocker wired GPIO14 ↔ GND with the 10k pull-up, leak probe 10k/4.7k on GPIO7, divider on GPIO4. Never connect the 3S pack to the DevKit's own LiPo connector (BAT_SENS GPIO6 is the board's 1S cell). Log with bench_log.py --card C027; the calibration factor it prints goes into the firmware config with // SOURCE: C027. This is the battery and leak half of the safety (T2).
cards.title: Ladder bench: battery divider, leak probe and KILL rocker on the DevKit

cards.label: C029
cards.hyp: With Pesho's head at 37 °C (50 ml bottle or warmer, checked with the Laserliner) 1.0 m in front of the camera in a room at ~22 °C, the `mlx90640` env shows max_C ≥ 30 °C at the hot pixel and hot_x/hot_y move when the head moves left/right; the hot spot is ≥ 2 pixels at 1 m.
cards.note: When the camera arrives (BOM row 77, dispatched). Sketch exists (T3, env `mlx90640`, I2C-1 GPIO8/9 @0x33, 4 Hz). `scan` first: 0x33 must answer. Measure the head with the IR thermometer at the same time (12:1 → hold 30 cm for a 2.5 cm spot), write both numbers. Then 2 m and 3 m: at what distance does the hot spot fall under 2 px? That number goes into the mission search range. Log with bench_log.py --card C029; screenshot of the heat map. The D45 camera gets its own card when it arrives.
cards.title: MLX90640 110° on the bench: does it see Pesho at 37 °C from 1 m?

cards.label: C030
cards.hyp: EXT1 and EXT2 are 2 × 22 pins at 2.54 mm; the row spacing measured with inner/outer edges matches the Olimex drawing within 0.1 mm; header pin 1 of EXT1 is 3V3 and pin 22 GND as in PINOUT.md; after C015 and C006 every VERIFY line in the DevKit-Lipo table is either SOURCE or deleted.
cards.note: Decision 0005. Everything the perfboard (C031) and the Aisler carrier (C032) need: 1) caliper on the DevKit: row spacing EXT1 ↔ EXT2 (pins of the same number, inner edges A + outer edges B, c-c = (A+B)/2), board outline, mounting holes, where USB-C and the LiPo connector sit (they must stay reachable). 2) Count the header pins with the meter: EXT1 pin 1 = 3V3? pin 22 = GND? 3) Results in: C015 (GPIO39 pull-downs yes/no), C006 (ESC signal level → level shifter yes/no), BTS IS pins used or not, PCA9685 channels for the 2 cradle servos (C023). 4) Claude updates PINOUT.md + pins_devkit.h (Cursor commits). Photo: caliper across the rows, top and bottom of the board.
cards.result: PART 1, 10.10 21:49 (6 photos, DevKit in the breadboard): rows EXT1↔EXT2 outer 26.69 / inner 24.50 → 25.6 by caliper; the board sits in a 2.54 breadboard across the channel, so the true spacing is on the grid: 25.40 (10 × 2.54). Along a row pin 1→pin 22: outer 53.77 / inner 52.84 → 53.31 = 21 × 2.54 (53.34) → 22 pins at 2.54 confirmed. Board 55.88 × 28.09 (2.2 × 1.1 in). Seen in the photos: 2 × USB-C (USB-OTG1, USB-UART1) on one short edge, the WROOM antenna on the other short edge (overhangs the PCB), LiPo BAT1 and pUEXT1 connectors and the RST1/BUT1 buttons on top, no mounting holes seen. PART 2, 11.10 03:38, continuity, unpowered, counted from the antenna end: EXT1 1↔EXT1 2 beep (3V3), EXT1 22↔EXT2 1 beep (GND), EXT2 1↔EXT2 22 beep (GND), EXT1 1↔EXT1 22 no beep (no 3V3–GND short) → header numbering anchors match PINOUT. PART 3, 04:01: `ladder` env flashed over USB-OTG1 (left USB-C, antenna up) → green LED (GPIO38) blinks 1 Hz — the first night-task bench sketch running on real hardware. PART 4, 04:05: meter DC V on EXT2 pin 10 ↔ GND swings with the LED → GPIO38 is EXT2 pin 10 as in PINOUT: signal-pin numbering confirmed (so GPIO39–42 = EXT2 9–6). Reference: screenshot 03:13 of the Olimex EXT1/EXT2 drawing → C030_01 in iCloud 01_Loops/C030_2026-10-11_devkit-pinout (Olimex's drawing, not for the portfolio). STILL OPEN: C015, C006.
cards.title: Freeze the DevKit-Lipo pinout before the perfboard and the PCB

cards.label: C031
cards.hyp: With the DevKit OUT: no short between 5V, 3V3 and GND (meter), every connector pin beeps through to the header pin in the layout; with 5.0 V from the bench supply the 3V3 rail stays absent (it comes from the DevKit). With the DevKit IN: the `ladder` and `pca9685` bench envs run unchanged and `scan` finds 0x40 (and 0x28 / 0x33 when fitted).

Logs with bench_log.py --card C031.

cards.label: C032
cards.note: Decision 0005, same nets as the perfboard (C031). 1) Claude writes pcb/carrier-revB/SPEC.md from the frozen pinout (C030): board size, DevKit on female headers, JST-XH on the edges, test points, silkscreen 'AR-Mini carrier rev B · <date>'. 2) KiCad 9: board generated like rev 0, then Teddy runs DRC until 0 errors (rev 0 took 3 rounds). 3) Pre-order ritual: print the board 1:1 on paper, lay the DevKit and a JST-XH housing on it — every pin on its pad. 4) Send the .kicad_pcb (not the .scad!) to Aisler, 3 pcs, 2 layers, 1.6 mm. cards.label: C023
cards.note: For R1b both cradle servos must move together, the right one mirrored. Task for Cursor (daytime, small): in firmware/bench pca9685 add `pair <chA> <chB> <deg> [deg_per_s]` — chB gets the mirrored pulse (us_B = 3000 − us_A around 1500), ramp default 20°/s, `dm` dead-man and `kill` work as for the other commands; host test for the mirror math; README + PROTOCOL updated. Channels: CH0/1 ESCs, CH2–5 BTS7960, CH6 buzzer, CH7–9 LEDs → use CH10/CH11, VERIFY in hardware/wiring/PINOUT.md. TD-8120MG: 500–2500 µs, 180°. Servo power from the Jesverty at 6.0 V, CC 3 A — NOT 12 V. First run with the linkages off the servos, then with the arms on and the U empty, then Pesho.

cards.label: C022
cards.note: For the full U both hulls are needed. 1) Right hull_fore: Cursor, OpenSCAD -D part="hull_fore" -D side=-1 → build/hull_fore_R.stl; print exactly like C008 (white PLA, 0.2, 4 walls, diagonal, tree supports under the 2 rim bosses only, ~6 h 13). Best slot: 11.10 after the C007 tub test. 2) 2 × arch_post: -D part="arch_post" (same part both sides), black PLA, lying on its side. Inserts M3 in both hull_fore bosses at x 165. 3) Arch tube: 15 × 15 × 1 aluminium, cut 304 mm (same as the beams), M3 bolt through post + tube on each side (square tube in a square saddle, so the hulls cannot twist). Check: gap between the hulls 250 ±2 at the front and at x 200, hulls parallel. Photo from above with a tape measure across.
cards.result: Step 1 started 11.10 15:45: right hull_fore printing, ETA ~22:00 (slicer ~6 h 13). It was mirrored in Creality Print (Mirror → Along Y axis) instead of exporting build/hull_fore_R.stl. That is the same geometry, because side = -1 in the CAD is mir() = a Y mirror. Same settings as C008: white PLA, 0.2, 4 walls, bottom 10, diagonal, tree supports under the 2 rim bosses, external spool. Steps 2 (arch_post × 2) and 3 (arch tube) still open.

cards.label: C028
cards.note: For r2c 'swims on remote'. The DevKit makes its own WiFi (access point), the phone opens a small page: throttle + turn sliders (differential mix to ESC_L/ESC_R), a big STOP, telemetry line (v_bat, kill, leak, heading when the BNO055 is there). Heartbeat from the page every 200 ms; no heartbeat for 500 ms → SAFE (the T2 safety rule) → both ESCs 1500 µs. WiFi password only in the gitignored include/secrets.h (secrets.h.example in the repo), never in git or the chat. Claude writes the spec in tasks/night/ first; Teddy starts it when C025 has passed.

cards.label: C033
cards.note: Step 3 of the controller ladder: 1) DevKit-Lipo (WROOM-1-N8R8 on a ready board) → 2) carrier rev B, DevKit on female headers (C031 perfboard, C032 Aisler) → 3) rev C, the module itself on the carrier. Have: 3 × ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (Comet, 05.10) — same chip as the DevKit, 16 MB flash instead of 8: the firmware only changes the flash size in platformio.ini. Rev C adds what the DevKit gives for free: 3.3 V LDO (AP2112K-3.3), 10/22 µF decoupling, EN RC 10 kΩ + 1 µF, BOOT button on GPIO0, USB-C with ESD (USBLC6-2SC6) and 2 × 5.1 kΩ on CC, polyfuse 1.1 A + SMBJ5.0A (list in FAILS_AND_FIXES numbers register, 05.10). Copper keep-out under the PCB antenna. Soldering: castellated edge pads ~1.27 mm + a large GND pad underneath → flux, fine tip, loupe/USB microscope, and hot air or via holes for the bottom pad — or Aisler assembly. One module for practice first. Storage until then: back in the antistatic bag with desiccant; Espressif MSL 3 — bake per J-STD-033 before hot air/reflow if they stayed out long. Not before the portfolio (1.11): the hardest joint of the project.
cards.title: v2 (after 1.11): carrier rev C — the bare ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 soldered on my own board
